findings.claim: --freshness ran only from the host's own copy of the checker, so the file being judged was the judge: a neutered checks-vendor.mjs under a regenerated manifest passed bare mode AND --freshness. The design's 'closes the hand-patch plus regenerated-manifest bypass at wave intake' held for 6 of the 7 members.
findings.evidence: a396ace: --freshness <clone> --bundle <dir> lets picasso's own checker judge a host dir; self-test pin RED before / GREEN after; end-to-end: 'refused: patched against upstream 1abfdef260: checks-vendor.mjs'. WIRING part A and SKILL 2a now name the clone-run command. The host-copy form still exists and is still self-certifying for the checker file — documented, not removed.

findings.claim: The --probe import scan missed a multi-line import whose clause carries a line comment containing a quote (e.g. `// it's ...`), so a non-bundle relative import in render-report.mjs — the one bundled file --probe never executes — could reach hosts with the battery green.
findings.evidence: a396ace: line comments with no quote before them on their line are blanked before scanning; self-test pin RED before / GREEN after; end-to-end plant now refused. First attempt (widening the clause class to [^;]) false-positived on the checker's own test prose and was reverted before commit. Remaining ceiling, marked 'ponytail:' in code: a quote inside a /* */ block comment in an import clause, or a // after a quote on the same line.

findings.claim: --export into a path that is an existing file crashed with an ENOTDIR stack trace instead of a refusal with a rule and a fix (nothing was written, exit 1).
findings.evidence: a396ace: 'refused: --export needs a directory; <path> is a file (nothing was written)' with a fix; self-test pin RED before / GREEN after.

findings.claim: --freshness from a clone with NO fetched tip (no @{upstream}, no origin/HEAD) prints 'FRESH FOR THIS WAVE' although the clone's recency is unproven.
findings.evidence: Justification: the tip rule is stallion's 'first fetched tip that resolves' law, mirrored on purpose (tools/checks-vendor.mjs comment above the tip loop); refusing when none resolves would refuse every detached checkout (a CI pull-request merge ref, a checkout of a sha), where neither tip exists; the verdict names the clone it judged. WIRING part A's intake step now says to pull the clone first and that a clone with no fetched upstream has nothing to be behind.
